Subject: ACME: Integration + Model Routing Policy (post-demo next steps)

Hi Sara — great call earlier, thanks for sharing ACME's goals and constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum.

Recap (short):
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + internal search with rerank; ~50 qps expected in peak, with spikes to 200 qps for batch reindex windows.
- Controls that matter: latency SLO (P95 target ~200ms), cost sensitivity on high-volume prompts, and EU data residency for EU customers.
- Integration surface: front-end calls -> Redwood API for chat/generation; embedding pipeline (batched) -> vector DB + reranker.

Action items / next steps:
1) Tech deep-dive with your infra/eng team (we recommend Dev + Rishi) — propose Wed Jul 17 10:00 AM PT. Please confirm.
2) Share integration checklist and sample routing/policy config (attached: integration-checklist + MA plan).
3) Security/compliance pack and regional deployment options (link in related links).
4) Procurement: Sara, you mentioned a 4–6 week procurement window — if you want an MSA/estimate, we can share a draft.

Key integration notes (high level):
- SDK & auth: we support REST + official SDKs (Python/Node). API keys for hosted; VPC private deploys use mTLS + KMS keywrap. We'll include code snippets for token refresh flow.
- Model routing: you can define policy chains by priority: e.g. 1) low-cost quantized variant for non-critical assistant responses, 2) high-accuracy model for expensive generation/summary tasks, with automatic fallback if capacity/latency exceeds thresholds.
- Latency/cost policy examples: route by P99 latency budget (if expected >250ms, route to faster model variant), and route by estimated cost-per-token for high-volume channels.
- Region routing: per-customer or per-tenant routing rule (EU customers -> EU region private endpoint; fallback to US-hosted only if explicitly allowed).
- Structured output & tool-calling: we support function/tool calling + schema validation; recommend using structured output mode for post-processing and traceability.
- Embeddings + reranker: two-stage flow: dense retrieve (ANN vector store) -> small++ cross-encoder reranker for top-K. We can host reranker in Dedicated pool for consistent latency.

Please review the attached checklist and the sample policy we'll email separately. If Wed 10 AM PT works, we'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Thanks — talk soon.

Marissa Cole

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Sara. A few technical clarifications ahead of the deep-dive: 

1) Region isolation: yes — for ACME's use-case we recommend either (a) a private EU deployment (VPC + KMS in-region) with strict tenant routing, or (b) Hosted with EU-only endpoints and policy enforcement in the control plane that prevents cross-region fallback. Option (a) is the stricter guarantee.

2) Sample routing policy (pseudo-DSL):
- priority: [latency_sensitive, default, cost_saver]
- rule latency_sensitive:
    trigger: endpoint.latency.p95 > 250ms OR user.intent in ["live_chat","checkout"]
    action: route_to: high_throughput_variant
- rule cost_saver:
    trigger: endpoint.predicted_monthly_tokens > 1e7
    action: route_to: quantized_budget_variant
- fallback_chain: [high_throughput_variant -> standard_variant -> quantized_budget_variant]

This gives you a prioritized chain where requests can fall back automatically based on configured thresholds. We'll share concrete YAML examples in the repo/Confluence before the call.

3) Embeddings + reranker: recommend batching embeddings at off-peak windows; for near-real-time search, use HNSW (ANN) with a small cross-encoder under a Dedicated pool for latency-stable reranks. We can provide a pre-built pipeline and sample TTLs for vector refresh.

4) Auth & SDK notes: SDKs support short-lived API tokens with refresh endpoints; for private deployments we use mTLS + KMS. We'll include a snippet for rotating keys and token refresh in the checklist.

I'll be on the Wed call and can demo a sample routing policy in the console. Rishi — can you join for the deeper infra Qs?

—
Dev
